title: Regulatory Evidence Copilot
thesis: Automate costly evidence review for regulated teams.
description: Regulatory Evidence Copilot is a software opportunity for Regulated mid-market companies that need to translate changing rules and policies into reliable operational work. The product would ingest official, machine-readable material, identify relevant obligations, map them to a customer's workflow, and produce traceable recommendations for expert review. Its primary buyer is the Chief compliance officer, while Compliance analyst teams use the service through a self-service application and API. The value comes from reducing repetitive evidence review, shortening response cycles, and preserving an auditable source trail. Subscription and usage-based pricing could support the delivery model. The system targets high automation and low marginal human effort, with people involved mainly for consequential exceptions. Initial validation should test buyer urgency, output accuracy, integration effort, repeat usage, and willingness to pay before committing resources to a production build. The proposed service remains fully digital in acquisition, delivery, support, payment, operation, and geographic scaling.

critical_assumptions.statement: An identifiable buyer owns the problem
critical_assumptions.falsification_condition: No role owns budget or accountability

critical_assumptions.statement: The buyer is willing to pay
critical_assumptions.falsification_condition: Observed behavior rejects the viable price range
critical_assumptions.validation_condition: Primary or observed evidence supports the price range

critical_assumptions.statement: The buyer is reachable through a repeatable digital channel
critical_assumptions.falsification_condition: No compliant repeatable channel reaches the buyer
critical_assumptions.validation_condition: A measurable digital channel reaches the buyer

critical_assumptions.statement: At least 90% of delivery can be automated
critical_assumptions.falsification_condition: Human work scales linearly with customers
critical_assumptions.validation_condition: Automation design keeps marginal human work sublinear

critical_assumptions.falsification_condition: Conservative gross margin is structurally negative
critical_assumptions.validation_condition: Conservative costs support positive gross margin
